title: The supported-Hom identification is the closed-support adjunction transpose
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-pc-scheme] and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Work on the small pro-etale site with constant coefficient sheaf $A_X$ and derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with $i_*$ the underived module direct image [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] and shifts $(K[a])^r=K^{r+a}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $C_i:D(A)\rightleftarrows D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A):R\Gamma_Z$ be the derived adjunction specified in [def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product], with $C_i(A)=i_*A_Z$ in degree zero; it is normalized there by requiring that the underived adjoint of $a:M\to\Gamma_Z(F)$, precomposed with the quotient $q_i:\underline M_X\to C_i(M)$, is the constant-sheaf adjoint of $a$ followed by $\Gamma_Z(F)\subseteq\Gamma(X,F)$. Let $F$ be a bounded-below complex of $A_X$-module sheaves and $a\in\mathbf Z$. Identify $H^a_Z(X,F)=H^aR\Gamma_Z(X,F)$ [def-pur-support-cohomology] with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(A[-a],R\Gamma_Z(X,F))$ by sending a class to the map carrying $1$ in degree $a$ to a representing cocycle. For $x\in H^a_Z(X,F)$ let $x^\flat:C_i(A)[-a]=C_i(A[-a])\to F$ be its adjoint under $C_i\dashv R\Gamma_Z$. Then the natural isomorphism $\chi^a_{i,F}:H^a_Z(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)}(i_*A_Z,F[a])$ of [lem-pur-supported-hom] satisfies
$$\chi^a_{i,F}(x)=x^\flat[a].$$
Equivalently, both identifications are derived from the same underived bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*A_Z,M)\cong\Gamma_Z(X,M)$, $\varphi\mapsto\varphi_X(q_i(1))$. No finiteness hypothesis on $F$ is imposed.

source.place: Step 5, "=\operatorname{cl}(f)\boxtimes\operatorname{cl}(g) by naturality and associativity of supported cup products": the supported cup product and the exterior product of classes with supports must read classes through the same supported-Hom identification (agent-formulated normalization).
